title: Why a positive test is probably wrong

probes.question: True or false: when a condition is very rare, most positive results can still be false positives.
Besides a test's accuracy, what else decides how much a positive result means?
options: How common the condition is in the people tested
How many tests were run last year

image.alt: Close-up of a handheld breath-alcohol tester with a black mouthpiece and printed operating instructions.

body.question: A breathalyzer wrongly flags 5% of sober drivers and never misses a drunk one. One driver in 1,000 is drunk. A random driver tests positive. How likely is it that they are drunk?
body.reveal: About 2%. Picture 1,000 drivers: 1 is drunk and tests positive, while about 50 of the 999 sober drivers test positive too. So only around 1 positive in 51 is real. When something is rare, false alarms from the many outnumber true hits from the few.
